bug_description.normalized: In the staged vulnerable gnutls checkout `ef3224c53b3a3ac51c7c1846cc3873fa1d4910f4`, the exact five-byte witness `58 6e 2d 2d 00` reaches `gnutls_idna_map`, which copies those bytes into a NUL-terminated buffer and calls `idn2_to_ascii_8z`. In the bundled `libidn2` checkout `ce0d453222ca51c056f4f442988710eb0b696365`, `_tr46` case-maps the resulting C string `Xn--` to the single ACE-style label `xn--`. The label has no bytes after the `xn--` prefix, so `_tr46` calls `u32_to_u8` on zero code points. The zero-length `u32_to_u8` branch returns a one-byte heap allocation and `ace_len = 0` without writing any byte into that allocation. `_tr46` immediately passes that pair into `_idn2_punycode_decode`. In `lib/puny_decode.c`, the zero-length-input setup block still evaluates delimiter/basic-code-point logic on `input[0]` with `b == 0`, even though `input_length == 0`. MemorySanitizer reports the resulting use-of-uninitialized-value at `/src/libidn2/lib/puny_decode.c:166:3`. The staged `patch.diff` is unrelated benchmark code and does not fix this path.

tainted_value_origin.description: Zero-length `u32_to_u8` conversion returns a one-byte heap allocation without writing any byte into it. On this path `_tr46` receives that buffer as `ace` together with `ace_len = 0`, so `ace[0]` remains uninitialized and becomes the MSAN origin.

sink.code:
for (j = b;  j < input_length;  ++j)
    if (!basic(input[j])) return punycode_bad_input;
sink.description: Exact staged crash location reported by MemorySanitizer. On the zero-length-input path, the post-delimiter setup block reads `input[0]` from the uninitialized one-byte `ace` allocation; the debug info attributes the use to line 166 in this block.
sink.note: The staged `reproduction_report.json`, `default_crash_trace.txt`, and `sanitizer_trace.txt` all report `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `/src/libidn2/lib/puny_decode.c:166:3` in `_idn2_punycode_decode`.

root_cause.description: The zero-length-input path is missing a guard before dereferencing `input[b]`: when `input_length == 0`, the function still evaluates `delim(input[0])` with `b == 0`.
root_cause.note: For the witness, `_tr46` derives an empty ACE payload and immediately calls `_idn2_punycode_decode(0, ace, ...)`. The initial scan leaves `b = 0`, no check rejects `input_length == 0`, and this statement reads the unwritten byte from the `u32_to_u8` allocation.

parser_admitted.condition: The staged witness contains a NUL byte (`58 6e 2d 2d 00`), so `_gnutls_str_is_print(input, ilen)` is false. `gnutls_idna_map` therefore skips the printable fast path and continues into the `idn2_to_ascii_8z` / `idn2_lookup_u8` conversion chain that reaches the saved crash.

fine_trace.note: Copies the exact five-byte witness into a project-owned string buffer and appends another NUL terminator. Because the copied bytes are `58 6e 2d 2d 00`, the downstream C-string IDNA logic sees the label text `Xn--`.

First libidn2 materialization of the attacker string. `u8_strlen(domain_u8)` stops at the witness NUL, so this converts exactly `Xn--\0` into a UTF-32 buffer representing the single label `Xn--` plus terminator.

fine_trace.code:
tmp[len2] = 0;
domain_u32 = u32_normalize (UNINORM_NFC, tmp, len2 + 1, NULL, &len);
fine_trace.note: The immediately preceding TR46 mapping pass rewrites ASCII letters to their mapped form before this normalization. For the witness label `Xn--`, the uppercase `X` is case-mapped to lowercase `x`, so the normalized `domain_u32` label becomes exactly `xn--`.

The single normalized label matches the ACE prefix test. Its total length is exactly 4, so the derived payload length after `xn--` is `e - s - 4 = 0`, and `_tr46` requests a UTF-8 conversion of zero code points.

Called from `_tr46` with zero code points. The zero-length branch returns a non-NULL one-byte heap allocation and reports `ace_len = 0`, but it does not write any byte into that allocation, so `ace[0]` remains uninitialized. MSAN's heap-origin stack points at this allocation path.

Immediately after step 5, `_tr46` calls `_idn2_punycode_decode(ace_len, (char *) ace, ...)` with `ace_len = 0`. The initial scan leaves `b = 0`, but this setup block still dereferences `input[0]` while trying to skip/check a delimiter even though the payload length is zero. Because step 5 never initialized the allocated byte, that read consumes poisoned `ace[0]`; MSAN attributes the use-of-uninitialized-value to line 166 in this block.

allocation_context.note: The saved MSAN trace reports the corresponding heap origin in `/src/libunistring/lib/unistr/u32-to-u8.c:119:33`; the staged bundled `u32_to_u8` implementation used on this path has the same zero-length `malloc(1)` branch at line 110.

format.name: 5-byte IDNA input to gnutls_idna_map
format.contract: The only verified trigger semantics are the exact five-byte blob `58 6e 2d 2d 00` (`Xn--\0`). `gnutls_idna_map` copies all five bytes into a NUL-terminated buffer, so libidn2 sees the C string `Xn--`; TR46 maps that to `xn--`, yielding a single ACE-prefixed label with zero bytes after the prefix. That exact zero-length ACE payload drives `u32_to_u8(..., 0, ...)` and then `_idn2_punycode_decode(0, ace, ...)`, which triggers the saved MSAN crash. The staged evidence does not justify a broader input class.
